entry.title: Ironwood · Day 2: The Girl Who Stopped Halfway Down the Road
entry.content:
Wednesday 4 July 2046, afternoon

IT'S YOUR HALL. DON'T LET THEM DECIDE WITHOUT YOU.Hall-vote leaflet, handed out at the Culvert Road junction

By afternoon the drizzle had stopped. Amara Nwosu left the bench at Linden Rise and set out with her meter for the Tangle, to take a reading off something other than the grate. At the Culvert Road junction a survey van with a council sign and Second Growth on its door stood across the pavement, and a clump of people were handing out leaflets about the hall vote. The needle jumped past its felt-tip marks. She could not get by without pushing through them, the box shrieking, so she turned back. Her hands shook all the way.

In Natalie's flat, Isabel asked her to come to the cuts and stay close, so she would know where Natalie was. Natalie said she was not going near the north cut, and would not say why.

The north cut was a blight Isabel had opened and left before its root was dead; left alone, a seam closes back over. Because it would not wait, Natalie asked Isabel to finish it now, with her watching. Isabel held up her hands. They would not hold, she said.

Natalie took her coat and went alone. Isabel watched her stop halfway to the north cut.

Nat stood with the itch at the back of her neck. Go on, and Iz sat in the flat alone with those hands. Girls left alone did not keep. The waiting was the part she knew.

She did not go on. The north cut's seam closed a little further over.

Log

  • Amara set out with her signal meter to the Tangle and got only as far as the Culvert Road junction, where a Second Growth survey van and a clump of people with hall-vote leaflets blocked the pavement, and her meter spiked and jumped until she turned back. (failure, risky, rolled 3 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu shaken
    • Amara's signal meter: now with Amara Nwosu
  • Isabel asked Natalie to stay close and come with her to the cuts, and Natalie said she wasn't coming to the north cut and wouldn't say why. (failure, risky, rolled 2 (one die))
    • Isabel now believes: That Natalie is pulling away from her and won't come to the cuts because of last night.
  • Natalie asked Isabel to finish the north cut and watch her cut, and Isabel said her hands wouldn't hold; Natalie got as far as the road between the flat and the north cut before she was stopped, and the north cut's seam closed a little further over. (failure, risky, rolled 2 (one die))
    • The north cut's seam closes over +1
    • Natalie now believes: That Iz's hands are shaking too badly to cut, and she won't go to the north cut today.

entry.title: Ironwood · Day 1: The Answer Given in Daylight on the Canal Bank
entry.content:
Wednesday 4 July 2046, morning

DO NOT USE THE TOWPATH AFTER HEAVY RAIN.Council notice, cable-tied to the railing of the old canal bridge

The night's rain had pushed the drain lake at Linden Rise over its path and jammed the reeds against the culvert grate under the ring road. Amara Nwosu stood there with her half-built meter, a box for measuring the signal, the pressure blight put behind her teeth. The reeds had gone black at the root, and the needle jumped whenever she turned toward the grate. Isabel, whom she had asked for help, had not answered.

Across town, Isabel woke in Natalie's flat to an empty bed and the coat gone from the hook. Natalie had slipped out first, so that no one would ask where she was going. Isabel caught her on the bank by the old canal bridge. Natalie halted at her voice, because she had been seen.

Isabel made herself look at Natalie's face and asked whether last night still stood, in daylight.

"It stands," Natalie said.

Then why the bridge, Iz thought. Next time she would be up first.

Amara wrote again, asking to be shown how to cut a nerved blight down to its root. She left out the two cuts she had already made alone, so that Isabel would not refuse her. Isabel agreed to show her when they could meet. Amara turned the phone face down on the wet stone.

Log

  • The night's rain pushed the drain lake at Linden Rise over its path and jammed the reeds against the culvert grate under the ring road, while Amara's half-built signal meter kept jumping and Isabel still hadn't answered. (clean, risky, rolled 6 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu buoyed
  • Amara sent Isabel a second message asking to be shown how to cut nerved blight, without mentioning the two cuts she has already made alone; Isabel agreed to show her when they can meet. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 4 (one die))
    • Amara Nwosu ashamed
    • Isabel now believes: That Amara has never cut a nerved blight and is asking how for the first time.
  • Isabel made herself look at Natalie's face and ask whether last night still stands in daylight; Natalie said yes, it still stands, and Isabel could not read anything past the answer. (success-with-cost, risky, rolled 5 (one die))
    • Isabel shaken
  • Natalie slipped out of the flat before Isabel woke and got as far as the canal bridge, where Isabel, who had come looking for her, caught her on the bank above the black water. (failure, risky, rolled 1 (one die))
    • Natalie ashamed
    • Isabel now believes: That Natalie was slipping out to leave her, not going down to the water.
